---
title: "PRESS"
subtitle: "Possession Risk Estimate from Spatio-temporal State"
---

PRESS is a work-in-progress, physics-informed framework for estimating the discrete-time risk that a team loses possession during its current canonical action. It combines physics-based pass and carry components with learned action and destination choices. [@spearman2017; @spearman2018beyond; @fernandez2019] **own derivation**

## Motivation

This portfolio project explores expected possession value ideas, football tracking data, and a physics-based formulation of ball-drive likelihood. The goal is to package the research code into reusable components with reproducible examples.

The central question is: given the current game state and the player in possession, how difficult is it for the team to retain the ball? Pressure can constrain the carrier's options, raise interception risk, and affect action choice. PRESS adapts building blocks from pitch control and EPV research to express this question as a team-possession hazard over canonical action opportunities. [@spearman2017; @fernandez2019; @bekkers2025; @skillcorner-pressure] **own derivation**

## Canonical-action loss hazard

The risk unit is team possession, represented as a sequence of canonical actions across successive carriers. A successful pass is nonterminal: it continues team possession with the receiver. It ends only the passer's individual control, which is the separate endpoint used by xLoss. The current-action hazard is evaluable at any usable frame of the current carrier. Canonical action starts define benchmark opportunities; additional snapshots only enrich the descriptive profile. [@fernandez2019] **design choice** [@singer2003] **own derivation**

At frame \(t\), the branch risks are combined as

$$
h_t = P(\mathrm{drive}\mid s_t)r_{d,t} + P(\mathrm{pass}\mid s_t)r_{p,t}.
$$

The drive branch accumulates defender-specific loss probabilities under shared remaining survival mass. The pass branch averages pass-failure probability over candidate destinations. Action selection supplies the pass/drive mixture weight; the transition model supplies destination probabilities. [@cao2007listnet] **own derivation**

The [interpretation guide](interpretation.qmd) separates the frame of evaluation, the canonical action step and the retrospective possession summary. The [residual-risk vignette](vignettes/05a_residual_risk/05a_residual_risk.ipynb) optionally extends the local branches to the final individual-possession outcome. **design choice**

## Data and reproducibility

The analysis is built around the SkillCorner open-data A-League sample. Raw tracking files are not included. Component API examples use deterministic synthetic inputs; the BCOS case study, h cases and sample report also include frozen real-match outputs. Notebooks can be rebuilt with the pinned Python environment. See [data setup](data.qmd) and the [repository README](README.md).

## Scope

The survival view is retrospective possession difficulty, \(D_t=-\log(1-h_t)\), \(H_t=\sum_{j\le t}D_j\), and \(S_t=\exp(-H_t)\). It is not comparable to SkillCorner's forward-looking xloss. **own derivation**

Three report patterns—escape, drawing pressure and sustained successful carrying—use explicit project rules inspired by SkillCorner. The historical eight-label sequence helper remains a separate API taxonomy. **design choice**

See the separate [benchmark page](benchmark.qmd) for the five component evaluations, and the [separate composed-risk benchmark](vignettes/05b_composed_risk_benchmark/05b_composed_risk_benchmark.ipynb) for h and xLoss.

## Start using the package

Follow the [match → possession → frame guide](usage.qmd) or execute the [workflow vignette](vignettes/00_match_workflow/00_match_workflow.ipynb) without match downloads. Browse the [Python function reference](api.qmd), [scientific solver reference](solvers.qmd), and [package/portfolio action plan](roadmap.qmd). Initialization validates one match; getters select its team possessions, frames and action checkpoints; compute calls produce and store the requested quantities.
